357466.title: Non-almost-realizability conjecture for the partition numbers
357466.statement:
For $n\geq1$, let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$, meaning unordered sums of positive integers.

**Partition-number conjecture.** The sequence

$$
(p(n))_{n=1}^\infty=(1,2,3,5,7,11,15,\ldots)
$$

of partition numbers is not almost realizable.

This conjecture concerns the realizability framework developed for combinatorial sequences. The source motivates it by computational evidence, while its status remains unresolved.

357982.title: Hansen–Vukicevic's conjecture for commuting and non-commuting graphs of finite groups
357982.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian group, and let $\Gamma(G)$ denote either the commuting graph or the non-commuting graph of $G$. Its first and second Zagreb indices are

$$
M_{1}(\Gamma(G))=\sum_{v\in v(\Gamma(G))}\deg(v)^2,\qquad M_{2}(\Gamma(G))=\sum_{uv\in e(\Gamma(G))}\deg(u)\deg(v).
$$

**Hansen–Vuki\v{c}evi\'{c}'s conjecture for group graphs.**

$$
\frac{M_{2}(\Gamma(G))}{|e(\Gamma(G))|}\geq\frac{M_{1}(\Gamma(G))}{|v(\Gamma(G))|}.
$$

The authors report computational verification for commuting and non-commuting graphs of finite non-abelian groups of order at most $1000$. The conjecture remains open in the supplied text.

358422.title: The convex-drawing extension conjecture for plane Hamiltonian cycles
358422.statement:
Let $D$ be a convex drawing of the complete graph $K_n$, and let $C$ be a plane Hamiltonian cycle in $D$. A **plane Hamiltonian subdrawing** is a crossing-free subdrawing spanning all vertices.

**Convex-drawing extension conjecture.** Every plane Hamiltonian cycle $C$ in $D$ can be extended to a plane Hamiltonian subdrawing on $2n-3$ edges.

The conjecture asks whether every prescribed plane Hamiltonian cycle in a convex drawing can be enlarged to the target-size subdrawing. The paper reports that this holds computationally for convex drawings with $n\leq 10$, while the analogous assertion fails for general simple drawings.

362002.title: The pattern-avoidance inequalities conjecture for restricted-cycle permutations
362002.statement:
For each $n\geq 1$, let $a_n^{\{1,3\}}(\sigma)$ count length-$n$ permutations avoiding the pattern $\sigma$ whose cycle lengths belong to $\{1,3\}$, and let $a_n^{\{1,2,3\}}(\sigma)$ count length-$n$ permutations avoiding $\sigma$ whose cycle lengths belong to $\{1,2,3\}$. **Pattern-avoidance inequalities conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$, one has

$$
a_n^{\{1,3\}}(132) \leq a_n^{\{1,3\}}(321)
$$

and

$$
a_n^{\{1,2,3\}}(123) \leq a_n^{\{1,2,3\}}(132)\leq a_n^{\{1,2,3\}}(321)\leq a_n^{\{1,2,3\}}(231).
$$

These inequalities are conjectured from numerical evidence in the cited tables; the supplied text does not establish them or report a resolution.

362028.title: Coxeter-length difference under the Simion–Schmidt map
362028.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, let $
obreak\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)$ denote Coxeter length, and let the Simion–Schmidt map send a permutation to its image. The associated statistic is the difference between the Coxeter lengths of a permutation and its image.

**Coxeter-length difference conjecture.** The difference in Coxeter length of a permutation and its image under the Simion–Schmidt map (Statistic $123$) exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon under involutions with $2^{n-1}$ fixed points.

This is one of the conjectured instances of the cyclic sieving phenomenon in the paper; it was tested computationally up to $n=10$, but no proof or resolution is supplied.

362167.title: Eventual gonality conjecture for king's graphs
362167.statement:
Let $K_{m\times n}$ denote the king's graph on an $m\times n$ grid, with $4\leq m\leq n$. The gonality of a graph is denoted by $\operatorname{gon}(G)$. **Eventual gonality conjecture.** For $4\leq m\leq n$, we have

$$
\operatorname{gon}(K_{m\times n})=3m-2.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by computational evidence that the gonality is already $10$ for $K_{4\times4}$ and $K_{4\times5}$, although the stated formula remains to be established for the indicated family of king's graphs.

363220.title: Mixed nilpotent-soluble regularity conjecture for symmetric and alternating groups
363220.statement:
Let $G$ be either $S_n$ or $A_n$ with $n\geqslant 13$, and let $(H,K)$ be a pair of subgroups of $G$, where $H$ is nilpotent and $K$ is soluble. A pair $(H,K)$ is **regular** when it satisfies the regularity condition defined for subgroup tuples in the paper. **Mixed nilpotent-soluble regularity conjecture.** Every such pair $(H,K)$ is regular.

The conjecture extends known results that every nilpotent pair is regular for $n\geqslant 5$ except for $S_8$. It is motivated by computations in low degrees, and its general validity remains open.

364527.title: The unrestricted classification conjecture for periodic Golay pair compressions
364527.statement:
Let $(A,B)$ be the $(v/2)$-decomposition of a periodic Golay pair $\operatorname{PG}(v)$ with row sums $a$ and $b$. Equivalence is taken in the sense used for these decompositions. **Classification conjecture.** Then $(A,B)$ is equivalent to either

$$
([0,a],[0,b])
$$

or

$$
\bigl([\frac{a+b}{2},\frac{a-b}{2}],[\frac{a+b}{2},\frac{b-a}{2}]\bigr).
$$

The preceding theorem proves this classification under a restriction on the prime factorization of $v/2$; the conjecture is that the same conclusion remains valid without that restriction. In particular, the case $v=50$ motivates the conjecture because exhaustive search found no compression of the additional form suggested by the multiple representations of $v/2$ as a sum of two squares.

364967.title: Forest-cut conjecture for sparse graphs
364967.statement: Let $G$ be a finite, simple, undirected graph of order $n$, and call a vertex set a **forest cut** if it is a vertex cut whose induced subgraph is a forest. **Forest-cut conjecture.** If $G$ has less than $3n-6$ edges, then $G$ has a forest cut. Maximal planar graphs do not have such vertex cuts, so the density condition would be best possible; the conjecture is verified for planar graphs, and the paper proves the weaker bound that less than $\frac{11}{5}n-\frac{18}{5}$ edges suffice in general.

365061.title: Asymptotic density conjecture for Ulam words
365061.statement:
Let $\mathscr{U}_n$ denote the set of Ulam words of length $n$, and define

$$
\rho(n):=\frac{\#\mathscr{U}_n}{2^n}.
$$

**Ulam-word density conjecture.** The density satisfies

$$
\rho(n)=\Theta(n^{-3/10}).
$$

This conjecture is based on the enlarged computational data set in the paper and is presented as a proposed alternative to the earlier conjecture that the density tends to a positive constant. No proof or resolution is given.

367773.title: Conjecture on endomorphisms of antipodal non-bipartite distance-regular graphs
367773.statement: Let $X$ be an antipodal, non-bipartite distance-regular graph of diameter $3$. 369623.title: Main conjecture on limited prime power sums
369623.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number greater than $23$. A **prime power** is a number $P^k$ where $P$ is prime and $k\geq 2$ is an integer. **Main conjecture on limited prime power sums.** Every natural number $n>23$ can be expressed as a sum

$$
n=\sum_{i=1}^{m}P_i^{k_i},
$$

where each $P_i$ is prime, each $k_i\geq 2$ is an integer, and $2\leq m\leq 5$. The conjecture is supported by exhaustive computation through $10^7$ and sampled checks at larger values, but no proof is given; establishing the bound of five summands remains open.

370576.title: Nonexistence of product-type half-flag-transitive automorphism groups
370576.statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a $2$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ design with replication number $r$ and $\lambda\geq (r,2\lambda)^2$. An automorphism group of $\mathcal D$ is **half-flag-transitive** when it is transitive on points and on blocks but not on incident point-block flags. It is of **product type** when it belongs to the product-type case for the induced permutation action on the design. **Product-type exclusion conjecture.** Any half-flag-transitive automorphism group of $\mathcal D$ is not of product type. The conjecture is motivated by Magma computations for parameter values $v_0\in\{5,7,9,11\}$, which detected no such $2$-design; its general validity remains open.

371615.title: The asymptotic generating-triple count conjecture for prefix reversals
371615.statement:
For $n$ and integers $m,k$ with $2\leqslant k<m<n$, let $f(n)$ be the number of pairs $(m,k)$ for which the prefix reversals $r_n,r_m,r_k$ generate the symmetric group $\operatorname{Sym}_n$. **Generating-triple count conjecture.** As $n$ tends to infinity, 
$$
f(n)=\begin{cases} \frac{1}{13}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv0\pmod{4},\\[6pt] \frac{1}{9}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv1\pmod{4},\\[6pt] \frac{1}{10}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv2\pmod{4},\\[6pt] \frac{1}{7}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv3\pmod{4}. \end{cases}
$$
 This is based on computational experiments for $6\leqslant n\leqslant70$; the source provides no proof or resolution.

371911.title: Hilton–Zhao's vertex-splitting conjecture
371911.statement: Let $G^*$ be an $n$-vertex connected class 1 $\Delta$-regular graph with $\Delta>\frac{n}{3}$. A **vertex-splitting** replaces a vertex by two adjacent vertices whose neighborhoods partition the original neighborhood into two nonempty subsets; suppose $G$ is obtained from $G^*$ in this way. **Vertex-splitting conjecture.** Then $G$ is $\Delta$-critical. Hilton and Zhao proposed this conjecture in 1997. It has been verified in several denser cases, including $\Delta\geq \frac{3(n-1)}{4}$, while the full range $\Delta>\frac{n}{3}$ remains open.

372231.title: Existence conjecture for link-irregular tournaments
372231.statement:
Let a **link-irregular tournament** be a tournament in which the directed links of every pair of distinct vertices are non-isomorphic. **Link-irregular tournament conjecture.** A link-irregular tournament exists on $n$ vertices if and only if

$$
n\geq 6.
$$
